meta.title: Turkish B2
meta.subtitle: 1,197 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Turkish → English (see the Turkish, recall the meaning) and English → Turkish (see an English meaning, recall the Turkish). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1,197 words for level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: the Yunus Emre Institute's Turkish Proficiency Exam (TYS) certifies only B2 and C1 and publishes no vocabulary list. The scope of this deck is taken instead from the Turkish as a Foreign Language Teaching Programme (Türkçenin Yabancı Dil Olarak Öğretimi Programı; Türkiye Maarif Foundation, 2nd edition, 2020, approved by Turkey's Ministry of National Education), a CEFR-based syllabus whose B2 tables for secondary school (pp. 285–294) are organised in ten themes: people and events that changed the world, figurative language, Anatolia as an open-air museum, planning a career, studying in Turkey, the world of the future, an atlas of cultures, a warming planet, books and reading, and music. FROM A2 UP THE PROGRAMME LISTS NO VOCABULARY AT ALL: its A2 table says the vocabulary section was left out so as not to limit the level, and the B2 tables carry none either. What each theme gives instead is its suggested topics — biographies and historical events, idioms, proverbs, poetry and folk songs, Anatolia's historic and natural sites and travel writing, aptitude tests and the jobs of the future, the education system, housing, applications and residence permits, artificial intelligence and consumerism, wedding rituals and customs from birth to death, natural disasters, global warming and renewable energy, publishing, reviews and libraries, musicians, instruments and world music. So 168 of the 1,197 words were written for Folio for those topics, a theme at a time, and are Folio's choice rather than the programme's; 12 more are words its B2 grammar list itself names (oysa, varsaymak, şayet, hâlbuki, bilakis …). This is not an official word list and is not presented as one. No word taught in the levels below is repeated. The other 1,017 are the commonest words of everyday Turkish, from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles. The cards are ordered by that frequency, so the words met most often come first; the 11 two-word expressions, which a list of single words cannot count, come last. Turkish builds words by adding suffixes, and a suffix's vowel follows the vowels of the word (vowel harmony) while some stems change before it, so the card carries the forms that cannot be guessed, read from a dictionary rather than generated. 651 nouns show their plural and five cases — sessizlik: sessizlikler, sessizliği, sessizliğe, sessizlikte, sessizlikten, sessizliğin. 173 verbs show the third person of the present, the aorist (the general present), the past and the future — beslemek: besliyor, besler, besledi, besleyecek — the aorist's vowel being the one a learner cannot predict. Adjectives do not inflect and carry no forms. Real example sentences come with 1,185 of the 1,197 words, three apiece for 1,152, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Scope: Türkçenin Yabancı Dil Olarak Öğretimi Programı, Türkiye Maarif Vakfı, 2020 (ISBN 978-605-80438-2-4). Meanings, forms and parts of speech: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency ordering: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
